All 31 tests pass. I created `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/FastDatePrinterAgentTest.java`, a self-contained JUnit 5 test class (matching the project's existing JUnit Jupiter 5 usage) covering:

- Happy-path formatting of `Date`, `Calendar`, and `long` millis, cross-checked against `SimpleDateFormat`
- Time-zone handling: printer's configured zone overriding the `Calendar`'s zone, no mutation of the input `Calendar`, and the `format(Calendar, StringBuffer)` instant-based variant
- `format(Object)` and the deprecated `format(Object, StringBuffer, FieldPosition)` dispatch for `Date`/`Calendar`/`Long`, plus `IllegalArgumentException` for unsupported types
- Accessors (`getPattern`, `getTimeZone`, `getLocale`, `getMaxLengthEstimate`), `equals`/`hashCode` contract, and `toString`
- Null-argument edge cases: null locale falls back to default, null pattern throws `NullPointerException`, null time zone throws on format
- Pattern-parsing edge/error cases: illegal pattern char, oversized `X` token, all three ISO-8601 `X`/`Z` variants, 12-/24-hour midnight wraparound, two-digit field overflow beyond its padding, zero-padding, small/large year formatting, two-digit year truncation, literal text with escaped quotes, era/month/weekday text fields, am/pm marker, and an unterminated quote edge case
- Java serialization round-trip, verifying the transient `rules` are correctly reinitialized by `readObject`

Per the task instructions, no other files were modified. Lambdas, the diamond operator, numeric-literal underscores, and try-with-resources were avoided throughout, even though they're valid at `--release 8`, per your explicit syntax constraints.
